A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CHTs/CHTss research. Their main text, appendices, equations, tables and figures support reliable comparison, including matching material across renumbering and relocation.

before.justification: v2 reports original image-classification, machine-translation, language-modeling and zero-shot results, alongside ablations and runtime measurements.

after.justification: v3 retains original experiments and adds density-decay comparisons, sensitivity studies, statistical comparisons and zero-shot error analysis.

M1.justification: BRF initialization, soft removal and regrowth, the CH2-L3n predictor, sigmoid density decay, network percolation and historical-weight recovery are retained. Algorithm 1 is unchanged; the new experiments test existing components.

E1.justification: Appendix H newly uses C4 for the LLaMA-60M density-decay comparison in Table 13. The existing image-classification, translation, OpenWebText and GLUE/SuperGLUE dataset coverage remains.

E2.justification: GraNet and GMP join the retained image-classification comparisons in Table 1 and v3 Table 7, alongside new CHTss results. The translation and principal OpenWebText comparator sets are unchanged. The additional methods discussed in Appendix M are not evaluated.

E3.justification: v3 adds MCC to zero-shot evaluation and introduces controlled sweeps over pruning duration, initial sparsity, decay curvature and removal fraction. A new comparison spans six LLaMA sizes from 20M to 1B. These substantially expand the evaluation design, while the principal training-configuration tables remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendix H adds sigmoid-versus-cubic scheduler comparisons, curvature and initial-sparsity sensitivity, removal-fraction sensitivity, and analysis of when density decay helps across model sizes. Appendix L adds label-imbalance and MCC analysis to investigate misleading zero-shot accuracies. The earlier initialization, soft-sampling and precision analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Table 2 newly reports three-seed means and standard errors for most translation results. Appendix H introduces Wilcoxon significance testing across six model sizes, reported in Table 16. This materially expands statistical reporting beyond v2's existing MLP standard errors and zero-shot standard deviations; an increase from a specified earlier run count is not established.

E6.justification: Table 2 replaces many translation scores with seed-averaged results and changes rankings: at 95% sparsity on Multi30k, RigL versus CHTs changes from 27.63 versus 29.45 to 29.94 versus 28.94. v3 adds density-decay MLP results and substantial appendix results, including negative MCC at 95% sparsity. The 130M zero-shot table is removed; the 1B accuracy table is retained unchanged.

T1.justification: The ELM definition, link-score and BRF equations, density-integral derivations and complexity analysis are unchanged. The added MCC evaluation and significance tests do not introduce new formal definitions, proofs or mathematical derivations.

C1.justification: v3 removes the claim of superior zero-shot performance from the abstract, introduction and conclusion. These sections instead emphasize language-modeling parity and CHTs' LLaMA-1B perplexity advantage, already supported by results in v2. The proposed-method contributions and main image-classification and translation claims remain.

C2.justification: Appendix L identifies label imbalance and nearly constant predictions as confounds behind high zero-shot accuracy, qualifies generalization claims using MCC, and discusses insufficient pretraining budgets. Appendix H newly explains CHTss benefits through sparsity-dependent connectivity exploration and addresses cases where CHTs performs better. The existing hardware limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v3 adds a code-repository link in the abstract and statements about supplementary code and instructions. It also discloses a pretraining token budget and settings for the new analyses. Existing pseudocode, principal hyperparameter tables and A100 hardware information are retained.

R1.justification: New Appendix M adds seven related works, including BiDST, AC/DC, Powerpropagation, S2-SAM, SLaK, CHASE and NEURREV, with brief descriptions of their approaches. This broadens context without substantially changing the paper's positioning around Cannistraci-Hebb theory.

P1.justification: Existing prose and the core section order are largely retained. Changes include localized abstract, introduction and conclusion revisions, terminology and affiliation edits, new appendix subsections, and a NeurIPS checklist. The scientific additions do not involve extensive rewriting of the retained narrative.

P2.justification: The tabular presentation expands substantially: six new appendix tables appear, image-classification tables gain comparison rows, Table 2 widens to display uncertainty, and the 130M zero-shot table is removed. Figure 1 is re-rendered with revised labeling; Figures 2–12 retain their content, with several relocations.

improvement.justification: v3 substantially improves the validity of the conclusions by exposing label-imbalance confounds behind v2's zero-shot generalization claim, reporting near-zero or negative MCC, and withdrawing the headline claim. Translation uncertainty reporting and new controlled ablations strengthen the evidence. Some new prose still overstates individual results: Table 13's cubic 6,000-step result is worse than the fixed-sparsity baseline. This limited inconsistency does not outweigh the correction of a central unsupported inference.
